title: Mr F & Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine
text:
Decision
Mr F & Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine
From
Office of the Commissioner for Environmental Information (OCEI)
Case number: OCE-152231-X5P6X9
Published on 24 June 2026
Background
Scope of Review
Analysis and Findings
Decision
Appeal to the High Court
Whether the Department has established that it did not hold information coming within the scope of the appellant’s request, in accordance with article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations.
24 June 2026
Background
1. This appeal relates to a request made by the appellant on 30 May 2024 for the following;
“For the period 1-1-2022 to date, information of the work of the Felling Conditions Group (referred to in AIE 24 069) to include details on the composition of the group and the subject matters considered, to include:
A) Details of meetings, including Dates, Attendees, Agendas and Minutes
B) Reports
C) Consultations
D) Recommendations
E) A list of the current Felling Conditions
F) Previous modifications to conditions
G) Correspondence”
2. The Department issued its original decision refusing the request under article 9(2)(a) on the basis that it had already addressed this matter under AIE-24-178 which related to a request identical to the one made in this appeal.
3. On 19 September 2024 the appellant requested an internal review of this decision.
4. On 20 August 2024 the Department extended the time to provide an internal review decision under article 7(2)(b) of the AIE Regulations.
5. The Department issued its internal review decision on 19 September 2024 varying its original decision and granting 37 records in full to the appellant.
6. The appellant appealed to this office in September 2024.
7. I have carried out a review under article 12(5) of the Regulations. In carrying out my review, I have had regard to the submissions made by both parties. I have also examined the contents of the records at issue. In addition, I have had regard to:
a. the Guidance document provided by the Minister for the Environment, Community and Local Government on the implementation of the AIE Regulations (the Minister’s Guidance);
b. Directive 2003/4/EC (the AIE Directive), upon which the AIE Regulations are based;
c. the 1998 United Nations Economic Commission for Europe Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-Making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters (the Aarhus Convention); and
d. The Aarhus Convention—An Implementation Guide (Second edition, June 2014) (‘the Aarhus Guide’).
Scope of Review
8. In accordance with article 12(5) of the AIE Regulations, the role of the Commissioner is to review a public authority’s internal review decision and to affirm, annul or vary it. Where appropriate in the circumstances of an appeal, I will require the public authority to make available environmental information to the appellant.
9. The scope of this appeal concerns whether the Department was justified in refusing access to environmental information on the grounds that no further information was held by or for the authority concerned in the meaning of article 7(5) of the Regulations.
Analysis and Findings
Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations
10. Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations is the relevant provision to consider, where the question arises as to whether the requested environmental information or any further environmental information is held by or for the public authority concerned. It provides as follows:
“Where a request is made to a public authority and the information requested is not held by or for the authority concerned, that authority shall inform the applicant as soon as possible that the information is not held by or for it”.
11. This office’s approach to dealing with this type of case is to assess whether adequate steps have been taken to identify and locate relevant environmental information, having regard to the particular circumstances. In determining whether the steps taken are adequate in the circumstances, a standard of reasonableness is applied.
12. Article 7(5) of the AIE regulations allows a public authority to refuse a request if it does not hold the requested information. In order for a public authority to successfully rely on this provision, it must, among other things, provide evidence that it carried out adequate searches for the environmental information requested.
13. In its internal review decision the Department provided an overview of the searches undertaken, including the following;
“Following the assignment of this Internal Review request to me, I contacted [Named Grade 1 Forest Service Inspector]. [Named Grade 1 Forest Service Inspector] confirmed that the following searches were conducted in relation AIE 24 178: a search of the Department’s electronic repository eDocs; a search of email accounts of all relevant staff and a check of Shared Inboxes as set out in AIE request AIE 24 178. [Named Grade 1 Forest Service Inspector] also conducted a further search using the timeframe and keywords “Felling Conditions Group”, in response to the current request. This resulted in further thirty-seven (37) documents being located that are relevant to AIE 24 358, which I am now granting to you in full. [Named Head of Forestry Inspectorate] was also contacted by email and telephone and no further records were returned by him.”
14. During the course of the investigation, the investigator to whom the case was allocated, made a request for submissions to the Department which led to the Department conducting further searches. The Department noted that it contacted the [Named Grade 1 Forest Service Inspector] responsible for felling and who would have oversight of any felling conditions working group and [Named Head of Forestry Inspectorate] as the head of unit, who each conducted searches within their units in order to identify any further information. The Department noted that no further environmental information could be located.
15. In all the circumstances, in particular the Department’s explanation regarding the searches undertaken and the personnel who conducted the searches, I am satisfied that it has taken sufficient steps to determine that it does not hold any records further to the 37 already released to the appellant.
16. The AIE Regulations do not require absolute certainty as to the existence or location of records, as situations arise where records are lost or simply cannot be found, or, indeed, may have been destroyed in line with the body’s records management policies. The passage of time is also a relevant factor in such appeals. It is also important to note that this office does not generally expect public authorities to carry out extensive or indefinite general searches for records simply because an applicant asserts that more records should or might exist, or rejects a public authorises explanation of why a record does not exist. The test set out in article 7 (5) of the AIE Regulations is whether the public authority has taken all reasonable steps to locate the record(s) sought.
17. Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations does not require a forensic trawling exercise to be conducted by public authorities, rather a test of reasonableness and an adequate search exercise should be performed.
18. I am satisfied that on this occasion the Department has taken sufficient steps to determine that it holds no further environmental information relevant to the appellant’s request. Accordingly, the Department was justified in refusing the request based on article 7 (5) of the AIE Regulations.
Decision
19. Having carried out a review under article 12(5) of the AIE Regulations, I affirm the Department’s decision.
Appeal to the High Court
20. A party to the appeal or any other person affected by this decision may appeal to the High Court on a point of law from the decision. Such an appeal must be initiated not later than two months after notice of the decision was given to the person bringing the appeal.
Ger Deering
Commissioner for Environmental Information
respondent: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine
